source_refs.note: Exercise 4.1, Question 4: object thrown upward, air resistance proportional to velocity, and without air resistance; book p. 128, answers p. 303 (PDF 305)

blocks.prompt: 4 An object of mass \(m\) is thrown vertically upward. Assuming that the air resistance is proportional to its velocity at any time \(t\), construct a differential equation representing the velocity \(v\). Also, deduce the equation in the case when air resistance is negligible.
blocks.explanation:
A modelling question from mechanics: use Newton's second law, mass \(\times\) acceleration = total force.
Take upward as positive. Two forces act: weight \(mg\) downward and air resistance \(kv\) opposite to the motion.
steps:
Given: mass \(m\), thrown upward; air resistance proportional to velocity \(v\).
To find: a differential equation for \(v(t)\), with and without air resistance.
Method: Newton's second law \(m\frac{dv}{dt} = \) net force, with upward taken as positive.

The forces
Weight: \(-mg\) (downward).
Air resistance: \(\propto v\), so it is \(kv\) in size with \(k \ge 0\), and it opposes the motion: \(-kv\).
Why: air always pushes against the direction of motion; writing \(-kv\) gives a downward force while \(v > 0\) (going up) and an upward force while \(v < 0\) (falling).

Newton's second law
\[m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -mg - kv\]
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g - \dfrac{k}{m}v\]
Why: acceleration is \(\frac{dv}{dt}\); dividing by \(m\) leaves \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) alone.

Air resistance negligible
Put \(k = 0\):
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g\]
\[\dfrac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\]
Why: with no air resistance the only force is the weight, so the acceleration is \(-g\) (free fall).

Check:
\(v = \left(v_{0} + \frac{mg}{k}\right)e^{-kt/m} - \frac{mg}{k}\) satisfies the first equation, and as \(k \to 0\) it tends to \(v = v_{0} - gt\), which satisfies \(\frac{dv}{dt} = -g\) (both verified with sympy). The key prints \(\frac{dv}{dt} = -g - \frac{k}{m}v,\ k \ge 0\) and \(\frac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\). Agrees.
blocks.final_answer: With air resistance: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} = -g - \dfrac{k}{m}v\) (\(k \ge 0\), \(g\) = acceleration due to gravity). Air resistance negligible: \(\dfrac{dv}{dt} + g = 0\).
